Unit beings must be made to appreciate Its majesty.

paragraphs.text: Yama has five parts –(i) ahiḿsá, (ii) satya, (iii) asteya, iv) Brahmacarya, v) aparigraha.
summary: Yama has five parts –(i) ahiḿsá, (ii) satya, (iii) asteya, iv) Brahmacarya, v) aparigraha.

paragraphs.text: (i) Ahiḿsá: Not to inflict pain or hurt on anybody by thought, word or action, is Ahiḿsá.
summary: (i) Ahiḿsá: Not to inflict pain or hurt on anybody by thought, word or action, is Ahiḿsá.

paragraphs.text: (ii) Satya: The benevolent use of mind and words is Satya.
summary: (ii) Satya: The benevolent use of mind and words is Satya.

paragraphs.text: (iii) Asteya: To renounce the desire to acquire or retain the wealth of others is Asteya. Asteya means “ non-stealing.”

paragraphs.text: (iv) Brahmacarya: To keep the mind always absorbed in Brahma is Brahmacarya.

paragraphs.text: (v) Aparigraha: To renounce everything excepting the necessities for the maintenance of the body is known as Aparigraha.
summary: (v) Aparigraha: To renounce everything excepting the necessities for the maintenance of the body is known as Aparigraha.

paragraphs.text: Niyama has five parts – (i) shaoca, (ii) santośa, (iii) tapah, (iv) svádhyáya, (v) Iishvara prańidhána.
summary: Niyama has five parts – (i) shaoca, (ii) santośa, (iii) tapah, (iv) svádhyáya, (v) Iishvara prańidhána.

paragraphs.text: (i) Shaoca is of two kinds – purity of the body and of the mind. The methods for mental purity are kindliness towards all creatures, charity, working for the welfare of others and being dutiful.

paragraphs.text: (ii) Santośa Contentment with things received unasked-for is santośa. It is essential to try to be cheerful always.

paragraphs.text: (iii) Tapah: To undergo physical hardship to attain the objective is known as Tapah. Upavása (fasting), serving the guru (preceptor), serving father and mother, and the four types of yajiṋa, namely, pitr yajiṋa, nr yajiṋa, bhúta yajiṋa and adhyátma yajiṋa (service to ancestors, to humanity, to lower beings and to Consciousness), are the other limbs of tapah. For students, study is the main tapah.

paragraphs.text: (20) The major part of the slander in the world is based on falsehood. Some indulge in it unknowingly, some because their petty interests are hurt, and others, under the compulsion of hiḿsa vrtti (the mental propensity of harmfulness). chapters.title: The Body

paragraphs.text: (1) Keep the body neat and clean like a temple.
summary: (1) Keep the body neat and clean like a temple.

paragraphs.text: (2) After urination cleanse with water or by some other means.
summary: (2) After urination cleanse with water or by some other means.

paragraphs.text: (3) Twice daily before your regular meditation, and before any other time of meditation, bath or vyápaka shaoca (thorough cleanliness, half bath) must be done.
summary: (3) Twice daily before your regular meditation, and before any other time of meditation, bath or vyápaka shaoca (thorough cleanliness, half bath) must be done.

paragraphs.text: (4) Before taking food and before going to sleep, do vyápaka shaoca with cold water, or in cold weather, with lukewarm water.
summary: (4) Before taking food and before going to sleep, do vyápaka shaoca with cold water, or in cold weather, with lukewarm water.

paragraphs.text: (Method of doing vyápaka shaoca: At first wash your genital organs; then hands up to elbows and legs up to knees; then, taking a mouthful of water, splash water on the eyes and face at least twelve times. Finally wash the ears and the neck. Do násápána (flushing the nostrils with water) also (only if your stomach is empty).

For a sannyásii (renunciant) it is imperative to fast invariably on both ekádashiis, púrńimá and amávasyá.
